mainTopic: Which flaws disqualify a כהן but not an animal, and which disqualify an animal but not a כהן
overview: This amud finishes the משנה's list of מומין and then starts two new משניות. First, רבי יצחק shows that רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about extra fingers because they read one פסוק about a Philistine giant differently. רבה explains why each number in that פסוק is needed. After that, a story about רבי טרפון is told two different ways. The גמרא then explains the מחלוקת about a כהן who uses both hands. A new משנה lists conditions that disqualify a כהן but not an animal. The גמרא defines its words (כושי, גיחור, לבקן, קפח) and explains why a שכור fits in that list. The next משנה gives the reverse list: things that disqualify an animal but not a person. The גמרא explains how אותו ואת בנו fits this list, following חנניה. Finally, it asks how a כהן's vow to stay away from a forbidden wife can be kept from being released, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Both opinions on extra fingers come from one verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of extra fingers and toes. רבי יצחק says that רבי יהודה and the חכמים both built their views on the same פסוק about a Philistine warrior with six fingers and six toes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה mentioned someone with extra fingers on his hands and extra toes on his feet. רבי יצחק said: Both sides learned their view from one verse: 'And there was again war,' and it is written: 'And there was a man of great size, whose fingers and toes were six and six.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of extra fingers and toes. רבי יצחק says both sides of the מחלוקת learned from the same פסוק, and the next step will explain how.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה rules that a כהן with six fingers and six toes is כשר, while the חכמים rule he is פסול. רבי יצחק says the two sides do not have different sources. They share one source, the פסוק in שמואל ב about the Philistine giant at Gath, and simply read it differently.

keyTerms.meaning: They both learned from one verse
A man of great size, a giant or champion

phrases.english: [The Mishnah:] One with an extra [finger or toe] on his hands and on his feet.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. רבי יהודה rules כשר, and the חכמים rule פסול.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
And both of them learned from one verse,
'And there was again war,'
phrases.notes: שמואל ב כא:כ, about דוד's wars with the Philistines.

phrases.english: and it is written: 'And there was a man of great size,
the fingers of his hands and the toes of his feet,
six and six.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of the משנה's case of extra fingers and toes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both רבי יהודה and the חכמים base their views on the same פסוק about the six-fingered giant.

steps.title: Is the verse insulting the giant or praising him?
steps.stepSummary: One opinion reads the פסוק as describing the giant's flaws, so extra fingers are a מום. The other reads it as praise, so they are not a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds that the verse is speaking about his shortcomings. The other master holds that the verse is speaking in his praise.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק explains exactly how the two sides read the same פסוק differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים, who rule פסול, hold that the פסוק describes the extra fingers as something wrong with the giant, so they are a מום. רבי יהודה, who rules כשר, holds that the פסוק describes them as part of the giant's strength and power, so they are not a מום at all.

keyTerms.meaning: In his disgrace, describing his flaws

steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת over extra fingers comes down to one question: did the פסוק mention the giant's extra fingers as a flaw (so they are a מום, the חכמים) or as praise (so they are not a מום, רבי יהודה)?
steps.confusionAlert: Keep the sides straight. In this משנה it is רבי יהודה who says כשר (praise), and the חכמים who say פסול (flaw).

phrases.english: One master holds: it speaks of his shortcomings,
phrases.notes: The חכמים: extra fingers are a מום.

phrases.english: and the other master holds: it speaks in his praise.
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה: extra fingers are not a מום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the shared פסוק from Step 1 leads to two opposite rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading the פסוק as criticism makes extra fingers a מום. Reading it as praise means they are not a מום.

steps.title: Why does the verse give so many numbers?
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks why the פסוק needs to say 'six and six' and also 'twenty-four in number.' The total seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Why do I need what is written, 'six and six, twenty-four in number'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה asks why the פסוק spells out both 'six and six' and the total of 'twenty-four.' The next step gives his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each hand and foot had six digits, the total of 24 should be simple arithmetic. So רבה asks what each phrase adds, since the פסוק should not repeat itself for nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need (asking why something is written)

phrases.english: Rabbah said:
Why do I need that which is written:
'six and six, twenty-four in number'?
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק quoted in Step 1 (שמואל ב כא:כ), which ends 'שש ושש עשרים וארבע מספר'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to analyze the wording of the פסוק quoted in Step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the פסוק need both 'six and six' and 'twenty-four'?

steps.title: Each number prevents a wrong reading
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that both numbers are needed. 'Six and six' alone could mean six on only one hand and one foot. 'Twenty-four' alone could mean the digits were spread unevenly, such as five on one side and seven on the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If the Torah had written only 'six and six,' I would have said: six on his hand and six on his foot. So it wrote 'twenty-four.' And if it had written only 'twenty-four,' I would have said: five on this side and seven on that side. So it wrote 'six and six.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers his own question. Each number in the פסוק blocks a different mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Six and six' by itself could mean six fingers on one hand and six toes on one foot, with the other hand and foot normal (Rashi), so 'twenty-four' tells us each of the four limbs had six. 'Twenty-four' by itself could be a total made of uneven limbs, five here and seven there, so 'six and six' tells us every limb had exactly six.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed (both details are necessary)
I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)

phrases.english: They are necessary,
for if the Merciful One had written only 'six and six,'
I would have said:
six of his hand and six of his foot,
phrases.notes: Rashi: meaning only one hand and one foot had an extra digit, not both hands and both feet.

phrases.english: so it wrote 'twenty-four.'
And if it had written only 'twenty-four,'
I would have said:
he had five on this side
and seven on that side,
so it wrote 'six and six.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's question from Step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each number is needed. 'Twenty-four' rules out an extra digit on only one hand and one foot, and 'six and six' rules out an uneven split of five and seven.

steps.title: What the word 'in number' adds
steps.stepSummary: The word מספר teaches that the extra digits lined up with the others and could be counted along the hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In number' means that they were counted on the back of the hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה finishes by explaining the last word of the phrase, 'in number.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In number' tells us the extra fingers were real fingers in the same row as the others, so you could count them across the hand. They were not loose growths sticking out somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: On the back of the hand

phrases.english: 'In number': meaning they are counted on the back of the hand.
phrases.notes: The extra fingers sat in a single row with the others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבה's explanation of the פסוק by explaining its last word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'מספר' means the extra digits were in line with the others and could be counted along the hand.

steps.title: רבי טרפון blessed a man with 24 fingers and toes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה tells of a man with 24 fingers and toes who came before רבי טרפון. רבי טרפון said, 'May there be more like you in Israel!' רבי יהודה sees this as proof that extra digits are praiseworthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה said: There was a story of a man who came before רבי טרפון. He had extra fingers and toes, six and six, twenty-four. רבי טרפון said to him: May there be more like you in Israel!
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא records a story that רבי יהודה brings as proof for his view that extra fingers are not a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי טרפון blessed the man that there should be more people like him, extra digits must be a sign of strength, not a defect. This supports רבי יהודה's reading of the פסוק as praise and his ruling of כשר.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was an incident with one man
who came before Rabbi Tarfon,
with extra [digits] on his hands and on his feet,
six and six, twenty-four.
He said to him: May those like you increase in Israel!
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה understands this as a real blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאָדָם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the מחלוקת from Step 2 and brings a proof for רבי יהודה's side.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that extra fingers and toes are not a מום
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי טרפון's blessing to the man with 24 digits

steps.title: רבי יוסי: it was not a blessing at all
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rejects the proof. He says רבי טרפון actually said, 'May ממזרים and נתינים become like you, so that they dwindle away from Israel.' On this version, the extra digits are something bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to him: Is there a proof from there? This is what רבי טרפון said to him: May ממזרים and נתינים be like you, so that they decrease from Israel!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי pushes back on רבי יהודה's proof. He says the story actually went differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי, רבי טרפון's words were a negative remark. He wished that groups who are forbidden to marry into the community (ממזרים and נתינים) would have this condition, so that they would be recognizable as coming from unfit lineage, and people would not marry them. That way they would become fewer. If so, the story shows extra digits are a defect, which supports the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there a proof from there? (rejecting a proof)
נתינים, the Gibeonites, who are forbidden to marry into Israel

steps.whatToRemember: The same story is told two ways. רבי יהודה hears a blessing, so extra digits are a sign of strength. רבי יוסי hears a negative remark, so extra digits are a defect.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to him:
Is there a proof from there?
This is what he said to him:
Like you, may they decrease:
the mamzerim and Gibeonites from Israel!
phrases.notes: The wish is that these groups have this condition and become fewer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the story as a proof for רבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The quote was wrong. רבי טרפון's words were a negative remark, not a blessing.

steps.title: A ברייתא on left-handed and ambidextrous כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of one who uses both hands, then brings a ברייתא. A left-dominant person (in hand or foot) is פסול. For one who uses both hands equally, רבי says פסול and the חכמים say כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה mentioned one who has control of both hands. The חכמים taught in a ברייתא: A left-dominant person, whether in his hand or in his foot, is unfit. One who has control of both hands: רבי disqualifies him, and the חכמים rule he is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new case in the משנה and brings a ברייתא that lays out the rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds a point the משנה did not state clearly: a left-dominant person is פסול even if only his foot is left-dominant. It then repeats the מחלוקת about an ambidextrous כהן, which the next step will explain.

keyTerms.meaning: One who controls both hands, ambidextrous

phrases.english: [The Mishnah:] One who has control of both of his hands.
The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: אִיטֵּר, בֵּין בַּיָּד בֵּין בָּרֶגֶל — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: A left-dominant person, whether in the hand or in the foot, is unfit.
One who has control of both of his hands:
Rabbi disqualifies, and the Sages rule him fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: moves from extra digits to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A left-dominant person is פסול. For an ambidextrous person, רבי says פסול and the חכמים say כשר.

steps.title: Did the right hand get weaker, or the left get stronger?
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that an ambidextrous person learned to use his left because his right hand became weak, so he is פסול. The חכמים hold that his left hand simply became strong while his right stayed healthy, so he is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds: weakness began in the right hand. The other master holds: strength began in the left hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind each side of the מחלוקת about a person who uses both hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree on what we see: the person uses both hands equally. They disagree about the cause. רבי assumes the right hand weakened, which is a defect, so he is פסול. The חכמים assume the left hand gained strength, with nothing wrong on the right, so he is כשר.
steps.whatToRemember: Ambidextrous: רבי reads it as weakness in the right hand (פסול). The חכמים read it as strength in the left hand (כשר).

phrases.english: One master holds:
weakness began in the right [hand],
and the other master holds:
strength began in the left [hand].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the מחלוקת in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת depends on whether being ambidextrous comes from a weakened right hand (פסול) or a strengthened left hand (כשר).

steps.title: The משנה's list of conditions that disqualify a person but not an animal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists conditions that disqualify a כהן from the Temple service but do not disqualify an animal as a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A very dark person, a גיחור, a לבקן, a קפח, a dwarf, a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, a drunk, and people with skin marks that are טהור are all unfit if they are people, but fine if they are animals.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists conditions that make a כהן unfit for the Temple service but do not stop an animal from being offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some features count as a מום only for a כהן. A כהן standing before the public has to look fitting, but an animal only needs to be physically whole. Unusual skin color, extreme height or a mental state therefore disqualify the person but not the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: A person whose skin is extremely dark
A person who is not mentally competent
Skin marks that do not make a person טמא

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: a כהן can be unfit for reasons that would not matter for an animal קרבן.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: The kushi, the gichor, and the lavkan,
phrases.notes: The גמרא will define these three color terms.

phrases.english: the kipe'ach, the dwarf, the deaf-mute,
the mentally incompetent one, the drunk,
and those with skin marks that are ritually pure,
are unfit in a person but fit in an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of left-handed and ambidextrous כהנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These conditions disqualify a כהן but do not disqualify an animal קרבן.

steps.title: Two additional opinions in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a mentally deficient animal is not the best choice. רבי אלעזר adds hanging flesh to the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: an animal that acts like a שוטה is not the choicest kind. רבי אלעזר says: people with hanging flesh or skin are also unfit as people but fine as animals.
steps.whatsHappening: Two תנאים add comments to the משנה's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not say a שוטה animal is פסול. He only says it is not the best kind to choose. רבי אלעזר adds one more case to the list: flesh that hangs loosely from the body.

keyTerms.meaning: Flesh or skin hanging loosely from the body

steps.confusionAlert: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not make the animal פסול. He is only saying it is not the ideal choice.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹטָה מִן הַבְּהֵמָה אֵינָהּ מִן הַמּוּבְחָר.
phrases.english: A mentally deficient animal is not of the choicest.
Rabbi Elazar says:
Even those with hanging flesh
are unfit in a person and fit in an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds two more opinions to the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שוטה animal is valid but not ideal. Hanging flesh disqualifies a person but not an animal.

steps.title: First definition of the three color words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defines כושי as black, גיחור as white and לבקן as red.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A כושי is a very dark person. A גיחור is a very white person. A לבקן is a very red person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by explaining the three color words in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a first attempt at defining the words. The very next step will challenge the definitions of גיחור and לבקן.

phrases.english: GEMARA: A kushi is a black one,
a gichor is a white one,
a lavkan is a red one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains words from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כושי is black, גיחור is white, לבקן is red (a first proposal).

steps.title: A story shows the related word means white
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the definitions with a story. Someone offered 'לוקיאני' animals, and they turned out to be white.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? There was a man who called out, 'Who wants לוקיאני?' and the animals turned out to be white!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first definitions using a well-known story about how people used a word that sounds like לבקן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לוקיאני sounds like לבקן, and in that story it meant white. So לבקן should mean white, not red. That means the first definition swapped two of the colors.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that so?' A phrase that opens a challenge
A word for a certain kind of animal; in the story they turned out to be white

phrases.english: Is that so? But there was that man
who said to them, 'Who wants lukiyani?'
and it turned out to be white!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the definitions given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The definition of לבקן as red.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: How people actually used the word shows that a word like לבקן means white.

steps.title: Corrected definitions: גיחור is red, לבקן is white
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא switches the definitions. גיחור is red, and לבקן is white. Each is backed up by how people talk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: a כושי is black. A גיחור is red, as people say 'גיחיא red.' A לבקן is white, like that man who called 'Who wants לוקיאני?' and they turned out white.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and gives new definitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the definitions of גיחור and לבקן are swapped. כושי stays black. Each new definition is supported by an everyday expression.
steps.whatToRemember: Final definitions: כושי is extremely black, גיחור is extremely red, and לבקן is extremely white.

phrases.english: Rather: a kushi is a black one,
a gichor is a red one,
as people say: 'Gichya red,'
a lavkan is a white one,
like that man who said to them,
'Who wants lukiyani?' and they turned out to be white.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13 by switching the definitions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: גיחור is white and לבקן is red.
steps.terutzMaskana: גיחור is red and לבקן is white, as everyday speech shows.

steps.title: רב זביד defines קפח as very tall
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד teaches that a קפח is a very tall person.
steps.simpleTranslation: קפח: רב זביד taught that it means a tall person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next word in the משנה and defines קפח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This identifies extreme height as a מום for a כהן. The next step will ask how height can be a flaw when it is often praised.

keyTerms.meaning: A word from the משנה; here it is explained as a very tall person

phrases.english: Kipe'ach: Rav Zevid taught: a tall person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes on to the next term in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קפח means a very tall person.

steps.title: Height is praised in a verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו taught that הקב"ה is praised for defeating tall people, which shows that height is admirable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי אבהו taught: How do we know that הקב"ה is praised through people of great height? Because it says, 'I destroyed the אמורי before them, whose height was like the height of cedars.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב זביד: how can tallness be a flaw if the פסוק treats it as impressive?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse praises הקב"ה for defeating the very tall אמורי, so their height was a sign of strength and greatness. If height is something admirable, it should not count as a מום.

phrases.english: Is that so? But didn't Rabbi Abbahu teach:
From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is praised through people of great height?
As it says: 'And I destroyed the Amorite before them,
whose height was like the height of cedars.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב זביד's definition from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב זביד's claim that a tall person is blemished.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק treats height as impressive, so it cannot be a defect.

steps.title: The blemish is a tall, thin, ugly build
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the מום is not ordinary tallness. It is being tall, very thin and unattractive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The case is a tall person who is lanky and ugly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by narrowing what counts as קפח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Healthy, well-built height like the אמורי had is praiseworthy. The משנה is talking about someone who is tall in an unhealthy, stretched-out way that looks unpleasant. That kind of build is the מום.
steps.whatToRemember: Height by itself is not a מום. Only a tall, gaunt, ugly build counts as קפח.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It refers to a tall one who is lanky and ugly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בַּאֲרִיכָא שְׁמִיטָה סַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any tall person is blemished, which would contradict the praise of height.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a tall, gaunt and unattractive person is a קפח. Healthy height is praiseworthy.

steps.title: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: do not marry someone with the same extreme trait
steps.stepSummary: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ advises that people who share an extreme physical trait should not marry each other, so their children will not be even more extreme.
steps.simpleTranslation: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ said: A tall man should not marry a tall woman, or they may have an extremely tall child. A dwarf should not marry a dwarf, or they may have an extremely tiny child. A pale man should not marry a pale woman, or they may have an extremely pale child. A dark man should not marry a dark woman, or they may have an extremely dark child.
steps.whatsHappening: Following on from the traits in the משנה, the גמרא brings practical advice from רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ about marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The traits discussed here (height, shortness, very light or dark skin) are the same kind the משנה listed. רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's concern is that two parents with the same trait could have a child with that trait in a far more extreme form.

keyTerms.meaning: A ship's mast, meaning an extremely tall person
Finger-sized, meaning an extremely tiny person

steps.whatToRemember: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ advises against marrying someone with the same extreme physical trait, because the child may get it in an even stronger form.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
A tall man should not marry a tall woman,
lest a 'mast' (an extremely tall child) come from them;
a dwarf should not marry a dwarf woman,
lest a finger-sized child come from them;
a pale man should not marry a pale woman,
lest an extremely pale child come from them;
a dark man should not marry a dark woman,
lest an extremely dark child come from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: גָּבוֹהַּ לֹא יִשָּׂא גְּבוֹהִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the traits just discussed (height and skin color) with advice about marriage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People who share the same extreme physical trait should not marry each other.

steps.title: Why is a drunk priest in this list?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list (חרש, שוטה, שכור) and challenges it. A שכור ruins the עבודה, so he belongs with the blemishes that ruin the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the deaf-mute, the imbecile, and the drunk. But a drunk כהן makes the עבודה invalid! He should have been counted together with the blemishes that make the עבודה invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes words from the משנה and asks a question about them. It argues that the שכור is listed in the wrong group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of disqualified כהנים. With some, the עבודה is ruined (מחלל) even after the fact. With others, he should not serve, but if he did, the עבודה still counts. The Torah ties drunkenness to ruining the עבודה, so the שכור seems to belong in the stricter group, not in this milder list.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is mentally incompetent
Makes the Temple service invalid, even after the fact

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה's list is the milder group. A כהן in this group should not serve, but if he did, his service still counts. That is why putting the שכור here is surprising.

phrases.english: The deaf-mute, the imbecile, and the drunk.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, which the גמרא is about to question.

phrases.english: A drunk profanes the service,
together with the blemishes that profane the service
it should have been counted!

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁכּוֹר מַחֵיל עֲבוֹדָה, בַּהֲדֵי מוּמֵי דְּמַחֲילִי עֲבוֹדָה בָּעֵי לְמִיחְשַׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the physical traits discussed earlier to the next items in the משנה's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's placement of the שכור in the list of milder disqualifications.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A drunk כהן ruins the עבודה. Anything that ruins the עבודה belongs in the stricter list, so the שכור is in the wrong list.

steps.title: Drunk from something other than wine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a כהן who got drunk from other intoxicating things, not from wine. That kind of drunkenness does not ruin the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה means someone who got drunk from other intoxicating things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by narrowing the case. The שכור in the משנה became drunk from something other than wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that drunkenness ruins the עבודה applies to wine. A כהן who became drunk from other foods or drinks is unfit to serve, but his עבודה is not ruined after the fact. So he fits in the milder list.

phrases.english: With other intoxicating things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שכור in the משנה was drunk from wine, so he should ruin the עבודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שכור in the משנה was drunk from other intoxicants, which do not ruin the עבודה.

steps.title: This answer disagrees with רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this answer does not follow רבי יהודה. He holds that a כהן drunk from figs, milk, or honey who enters the מקדש is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: This does not follow רבי יהודה. A ברייתא teaches: if a כהן ate pressed figs from קעילה, or drank milk or honey, and then entered the מקדש, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a note to its answer. The answer only works according to the חכמים, not according to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the Torah's word for 'strong drink' as including anything that makes a person drunk, not just wine. For him, a כהן drunk from figs or honey is fully covered by the איסור and ruins the עבודה. So according to רבי יהודה, the answer in step 20 would not work.

keyTerms.meaning: And not in accordance with רבי יהודה
Pressed figs from the town of Ke'ila, known to be intoxicating

steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, only wine makes a drunk כהן ruin the עבודה. According to רבי יהודה, any intoxicant does.

phrases.english: And not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda,
as it is taught: if he ate pressed figs from Ke'ila,
or drank milk or honey,
and entered the Sanctuary, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer of step 20 by showing which opinion it follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a כהן drunk from non-wine intoxicants who enters the מקדש is liable. The answer of step 20 therefore follows the חכמים, not him.

steps.title: Flaws that disqualify an animal but not a person
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists conditions that would not disqualify a כהן but do disqualify an animal from being a קרבן: אותו ואת בנו, טריפה, יוצא דופן, an animal used for a sin, and an animal that killed a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These are fit in a person but disqualified in an animal: an animal that would violate 'it and its offspring,' a טריפה, one born by cesarean section, one with which a sin was done, and one that killed a person.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists problems that make an animal unfit for the מזבח, even though the same kind of thing would not stop a כהן from serving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous משנה (Step 10) listed conditions that disqualify a person but not an animal. This משנה gives the opposite list: things that disqualify an animal but not a person. These are not body blemishes. They are legal problems, such as the animal's history or condition, that make it unfit as a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The ban on slaughtering an animal and its offspring on the same day
An animal with a fatal defect
An animal born by cesarean section
An animal with which a sin (bestiality) was done

steps.confusionAlert: Here כשרין means 'fit for the עבודה,' not 'kosher to eat.'

phrases.english: MISHNA: These are fit in a person
but disqualified in an animal:
it and its offspring, a tereifa,
and one born by cesarean section,
and one with which a transgression was performed,
and one that killed a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the גמרא on the previous משנה ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אותו ואת בנו, טריפה, יוצא דופן, an animal used for a sin, and an animal that killed a person are disqualified as קרבנות. The parallel conditions do not disqualify a כהן.

steps.title: Priests disqualified until they change their ways
steps.stepSummary: A כהן who married a woman forbidden to him is disqualified until he vows to get no benefit from her. A כהן who makes himself טמא to the dead is disqualified until he commits to stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן who marries women in a forbidden way is disqualified until he vows not to benefit from her. A כהן who becomes טמא to the dead is disqualified until he accepts on himself that he will no longer become טמא to the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with two kinds of כהנים who may not serve because of their behavior. Each one can become fit again by making a firm commitment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are not body blemishes. They are penalties for sinful conduct. The disqualification ends once the כהן commits to change. A vow not to benefit from a forbidden wife pushes him to divorce her.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן who marries a woman forbidden to him, such as a divorcée
That he takes a vow forbidding himself any benefit from her
A כהן who makes himself impure through contact with the dead

steps.whatToRemember: Some disqualifications of a כהן come from his body. These two come from his behavior, and they end once he commits to stop.

phrases.english: And one who marries women by a transgression
is disqualified until he vows not to benefit from her,
and one who becomes impure to the dead
is disqualified until he accepts upon himself
that he will not become impure to the dead.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַנּוֹשֵׂא נָשִׁים בַּעֲבֵירָה פָּסוּל עַד שֶׁיַּדִּירֶנָּה הֲנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from animal disqualifications to a כהן's behavior-based disqualifications.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן in a forbidden marriage, or one who becomes טמא to the dead, is disqualified from עבודה until he makes a binding commitment to stop.

steps.title: What does 'itself and its offspring' mean for people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what case of אותו ואת בנו the משנה could mean when it says this does not disqualify a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה said 'these are fit in a person.' What does it mean by 'itself and its offspring'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the new משנה. It asks what 'itself and its offspring' would even mean when talking about people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For animals, אותו ואת בנו means you may not slaughter a mother and her child on the same day. The משנה says this is not a problem for people. The גמרא wants to know what the parallel case with people is.

keyTerms.meaning: The rule not to slaughter an animal and its offspring on the same day

phrases.english: Gemara: 'And these are fit in a person' —
what is meant by 'itself and its offspring'?
phrases.notes: Read the word in square brackets, אותו, instead of the one in round brackets, באותו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה quoted in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What human case parallels the animal law of אותו ואת בנו?

steps.title: First try: אהרן and his sons — but the rule does not apply to males
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the case is אהרן and his sons serving on the same day. But then the parallel would be a male goat and its son, and a בריתא says the rule does not apply to males.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means אהרן and his sons, then the matching animal case is a male goat and its son. Does the rule apply there? But a בריתא teaches: 'itself and its offspring' applies to females and does not apply to males!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first answer, then immediately knocks it down using a בריתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father and son כהן may both serve on the same day, so that fits 'fit in a person.' But the matching animal case would be a father animal and its son. The בריתא says the animal rule only covers a mother and her child, so the comparison breaks down.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion about to be tested)

steps.confusionAlert: The animal rule of אותו ואת בנו, according to this בריתא, is about a mother and her offspring, not a father and his offspring.

phrases.english: If you say it means Aaron and his sons,
then the matching case is a male goat and its son —
does the rule apply there?
But it is taught: 'itself and its offspring' applies to females,
and does not apply to males!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to step 24 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the משנה means אהרן and his sons
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The matching animal case would be a father and son, but the בריתא says the rule only applies to females.

steps.title: Second try: a mother goat — but there is no female כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a mother goat and her child instead. But then the human parallel would be a female כהן and her son, and a woman never does the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means a female goat and her child. Then the matching case here is a כהנת and her son. But is a כהנת fit for the עבודה at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second answer, and that one also fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Switching to a mother animal fixes the בריתא problem. But now the human side must be a mother and her son. A woman never does the עבודה, so it makes no sense to say she is 'fit' to serve.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to do the Temple service

phrases.english: Rather, it means a female goat and her child;
then the matching case here is a female priest and her son —
is a female priest fit for the service?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 25 fails, tries a different answer and rejects it too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the משנה means a mother animal and her child
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The human parallel would be a female כהן, but women never do the עבודה.

steps.title: Back to the first answer: אהרן and his sons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the first answer: the משנה really means אהרן and his sons, matching a male goat and its son.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it means אהרן and his sons, and the matching case here is a male goat and its son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first answer. It is setting up the next step, which will solve the problem from the בריתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לעולם tells us the גמרא is keeping its original idea. It still needs to explain the בריתא that said the rule does not apply to males.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (returning to an earlier idea)
אהרן and his sons — a father and son כהן

phrases.english: Actually, it means Aaron and his sons,
and the matching case here is a male goat and its son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the answer rejected in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Returning to the first answer, with a fix coming in the next step
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first answer seemed to fail because of the בריתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה does mean אהרן and his sons.

steps.title: The משנה follows חנניה, who applies the rule to males
steps.stepSummary: Scholars in ארץ ישראל, quoting רבי יוסי בר אבין, say the משנה follows חנניה, who holds that אותו ואת בנו applies to males and females.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said in the West in the name of רבי יוסי בר אבין: This shows the משנה is חנניה. As it is taught: 'itself and its offspring' applies to females and not to males. חנניה says: it applies to males and females.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the problem with the בריתא. It says our משנה follows a different תנא, חנניה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the בריתא says the rule only applies to a mother. חנניה disagrees and says it applies to a father too. If our משנה follows חנניה, then a male goat and its son is a real case, and the comparison to אהרן and his sons works.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's case is אהרן and his sons: a father and son כהן may serve on the same day, but a father animal and its son may not be slaughtered on the same day. This follows חנניה.

phrases.english: They said in the West
in the name of Rabbi Yosei bar Avin:
This shows it is the view of Ḥananya,
as it is taught: 'itself and its offspring' applies to females
and does not apply to males;
Ḥananya says: it applies to males and females.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 27 by answering the בריתא from step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule applies only to a mother animal, so the משנה cannot mean a father and son.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows חנניה, who applies the rule to males too.

steps.title: A כהן in a forbidden marriage in the middle of the service
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה about a כהן who married a forbidden woman, a בריתא teaches that if this comes up during his עבודה, he vows, keeps serving, then goes down and divorces her.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who marries women,' etc. A בריתא teaches: He vows and serves; he goes down and divorces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and brings a בריתא with practical details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said this כהן is disqualified until he vows to get no benefit from the woman. The בריתא adds that the vow alone lets him finish the עבודה right away. After he finishes and comes down, he must actually divorce her.

keyTerms.meaning: He makes a vow (to get no benefit from her)

phrases.english: 'And one who marries women,' etc.
It was taught: he vows and serves;
he goes down and divorces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the משנה's ruling from step 23 and adds a בריתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow is enough to let him finish the עבודה, but afterward he must divorce her.

steps.title: What if he gets a sage to cancel his vow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא worries that the כהן might go to a חכם and have his vow (not to benefit from his wife) released, so he would never actually divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry: maybe he will go to a sage and the sage will release his vow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule from the last step. That rule relied on his vow not to benefit from her, but a vow can sometimes be canceled by a חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule let the כהן keep serving because his vow guarantees he will divorce the forbidden wife. If a חכם can undo the vow, that guarantee is gone. Then he could stay married to her, so letting him serve on the strength of the vow seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage who has the power to release vows
Releases (permits) it for him, meaning cancels the vow

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the husband's power to cancel his wife's vows. Here the worry is that a חכם will release the man's own vow.

phrases.english: But let us be concerned that perhaps he will go
to a sage, and he will release it for him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reliance on the vow in Step 29
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the כהן vows not to benefit from her and keeps serving before he actually divorces
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A vow that can be released by a חכם is not a reliable guarantee that he will divorce her

steps.title: He must explain the vow, so no sage will release it
steps.stepSummary: The תנא holds that a person asking to have a vow released must explain the vow to the חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: one must spell out the details of the vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the author of the ברייתא holds you must tell the חכם the details of your vow. Once the חכם hears that this vow is about leaving a forbidden wife, he will not release it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The power to release a vow is not automatic. The חכם judges each case. If the person must give the details, the חכם will see that releasing this vow would let the כהן stay with a forbidden woman, and he will refuse.

keyTerms.meaning: To spell out the details of the vow

phrases.english: He holds: one must delineate the vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry of Step 30
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the תנא's view on a related dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן could quietly get the vow released
steps.terutzMaskana: He must reveal the vow's content, and no חכם would release a vow like this

steps.title: What about the view that he need not explain the vow?
steps.stepSummary: The answer works only for the view that he must explain the vow. What about the view that he does not have to?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works out well for the one who says one must spell out the vow. But for the one who says one need not spell out the vow, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. The last answer depends on one side of a dispute, so it asks how the rule works for the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some hold that a person may ask a חכם to release a vow without saying what it was about. By that view the חכם would not know the vow concerns a forbidden wife, and he might release it. So the original worry comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well according to the one who says
What is there to say? (asking how the other view explains it)

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says
one must delineate the vow,
but according to the one who says
one need not delineate the vow,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר צָרִיךְ לְפָרֵט אֶת הַנֶּדֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 31's answer as covering only one view
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that he must explain the vow to the חכם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the opposing view he does not reveal the vow's content, so a חכם might release it

steps.title: The vow is made in public
steps.stepSummary: We have the כהן take the vow in front of many people, and a public vow cannot be released.
steps.simpleTranslation: That we make him vow in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the כהן is made to take his vow publicly, in front of many people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to one view (step 34 shows it is disputed), a vow made in public cannot be released. So even if he does not have to explain the vow to the חכם, nobody can cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: We make him take a vow
In public, in front of many people

phrases.english: That we administer the vow to him in public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 32
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a detail about how the vow is taken
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without explaining the vow, he could get it released
steps.terutzMaskana: A public vow cannot be released, so the guarantee holds

steps.title: What about the view that a public vow can be released?
steps.stepSummary: The public-vow answer works only for the view that a public vow cannot be released. What about the view that it can?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works out well for the one who says a vow made in public cannot be released. But for the one who says it can be released, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: Using the same pattern again, the גמרא says the public-vow answer also depends on a dispute. It asks about the view that even a public vow can be released.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer of Step 33 relied on the rule that a public vow cannot be undone. Some disagree and say it can be undone. By their view the original worry returns again.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow that was made in public
Cancellation of a vow (here meaning release by a חכם)

steps.confusionAlert: Usually הֲפָרָה means a husband or father cancelling a vow. Here it is used loosely for a חכם releasing a vow.

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says
a vow that was taken in public
has no nullification,
but according to the one who says
it has nullification,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר נֶדֶר שֶׁהוּדַּר בְּרַבִּים אֵין לוֹ הֲפָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 33's answer as covering only one view
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the vow is made in public
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the view that a public vow can be released, making it public does not protect the vow

steps.title: The answer begins: we make him vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its next answer with how the vow is taken. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: That we make him vow… (the answer continues on the next part of the daf).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the last challenge by again describing the way we make the כהן take the vow. This passage cuts off in the middle, so the full answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer will add a further detail about how the vow is taken, so that it cannot be released even by the view of Step 34. Wait for the next passage to see that detail.

phrases.english: That we administer the vow (continued on the next amud)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to Step 34
steps.terutzResolutionType: A further detail about how the vow is taken (completed on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even a public vow could be released
steps.terutzMaskana: To be completed on the next amud
